_about: The spec of kitcut.ai's open house invitation template (studio/templates.py make --spec). Its film is projects/open-house-invitation (local: the builder's logo and photos are third-party), pulled with studio/template_from_film.py from studio film studio-20261003-220824-nkmkf2: Lennar's grand opening of the Driftwood model home at Pepperwood, Stuart, Florida (Sat Oct 17 2026, 12-4 PM; lennar.com). Proven pixel-identical to the film. Redesigned 2026-10-05 (v3): one large card carries the film (the picture over a caption strip), every layout is worked out from the frame, and it holds in 16:9, 1:1 and 9:16; the v3 film is no longer pixel-identical to the studio film it started from.
title: Open house invitation
description: A 30-second narrated open house invitation. A yard sign swings in with the host's logo, the day and the hours, beside the home's name; then one large card carries the film: the home's photo with the day on it and its address under it; its bedrooms, bathrooms, square feet and price ticking in, each in its own place under the photo; two or three more photos, each with its room's name; the card shrinking onto a drawn street map as the pin drops on the host's street; and an end card with the day, the hours, the address and who to call.
author: KitCut
example: Open house this Saturday, 1 to 4 PM, at 12 Oak Lane, Austin: 4 beds, 3 baths, 2,450 sq ft, $685,000. Photos of the house and my logo are attached.
brief:
The film invites people to ONE open house, model-home opening or showing. Six narration lines, one scene each: the invitation (the yard sign and the home's name); the day and hours; the facts; the rooms; where it is (the map); the goodbye and the end card.

THE DAY IS REAL AND STILL TO COME. day ('Saturday, October 17'), dayShort ('Sat, Oct 17') and hours ('12–4 PM') come from the person's words or the event's own page, with the weekday the calendar gives that date: work it out, never copy a weekday on trust. An event that has already happened is not the one to invite people to: look for the host's next one, and when there is none, or no day is given, leave day, dayShort and hours "" (the sign then shows the kicker alone, and the narration says to check the page for the date). Never guess a day.

content.json (SK.DATA.content): logo: the host's logo (the agent's, the brokerage's or the builder's), a picture key; invite ('You're invited'); kicker: what kind of event, in the host's words ('Open house', 'Model grand opening'); home: the home's name or its street address when it has no name; homeSub: one short line under it, or ""; venue: where to arrive if it is not the home itself, or ""; street, cityZip, mapStreet (the street's name as a map writes it); contact: who to call or the agent's name and phone, only as published; facts: 0 to 4 {value, label} of bedrooms, bathrooms, square feet and price, only those given, each value as the listing writes it and each label one or two words (they stand in a row under the picture, one size for all). hero {img, crop, fx, fy, lift}: the home's EXTERIOR (an interior only when no exterior exists), shown large: img is a picture key; crop [x, y, w, h] (optional) is the part of the picture to use, in its pixels, when the picture is a page or carries a border; fx [from, to] pans across it (0 left, 1 right; [0.5, 0.5] to hold), fy (0 top to 1 bottom, default 0.5) says which part to keep when the frame is flatter than the picture, lift (optional, 1.1 to 1.35) brightens a dark picture. The picture is cropped to cover its box in every frame, so choose one at least 1600 px wide and keep the house away from its edges. rooms: 0 to 3 {img, label, fx, fy, crop} of interiors, each labelled with the room it really shows (a label of up to ~24 characters; longer takes two lines). With no hero the card shows the home's name in type; with no facts the address stays under the picture; with no rooms the exterior holds. Look at stills of the three frames after choosing crop, fx and fy. The photos are the person's own attachments first; else the host's own published photos of this home (the picture tool); with none, leave hero and rooms empty. Never use a photo of another home.

NEVER INVENT. Every fact is the person's own, from their words, their attachments or the event's own pages on the web: no made-up date, time, address, price, name, number or booth. A fact that cannot be found is left out (an empty string, or the item dropped from its list) and the layout closes over it. Use their real logo and their own colours and fonts: an attached logo first, else the one on their site (the picture tool), and name the picture's key in content.json. colors and fonts are theirs too, read off their site.

THE NARRATION sets the clock. Rewrite every line of vo.json for their event, keeping the number of lines and about their length, and record them with the voice tool. The scene cues at the top of film.js (SK.cues) hang on words of those lines: after rewriting a line, point each cue at a word the new line really says. Never read a URL or a phone number aloud; say dates and times the way a person would.

Keep the scenes, their order, the camera, the type and the sound. Long values are fitted by the code; check the stills after changing them.
